summary: Given the brief "Add logging to the app so we can debug production issues.", Claude invoked hyperpowers:brainstorming, ran a multi-question interview, escalated to the architectural path, wrote a 268-line spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-logging-subsystem-design.md, presented it for review with no implementation code, and after "looks good, go ahead" moved to hyperpowers:writing-plans.
reasoning: Session log shows Skill|hyperpowers:brainstorming as the first tool call, followed by repo reads, five AskUserQuestion rounds, a codex approach gate, the spec Write into docs/hyperpowers/specs/, and only after my approval a Skill|hyperpowers:writing-plans. No source files were modified at any point before approval (git status clean apart from a new .gitignore). Classification was architectural, not bounded or spike.

observations.description: Codex spec gate silently degraded: agent reported "the Codex spec gate did not produce a review. Preflight reported ready, but the resolved install is a 0.0.0-stub whose companion returns an empty result for both the approach gate and this one." Preflight claiming ready for a stub that returns nothing looks like a preflight-check defect.

The agent wrote a .gitignore containing `docs/superpowers` and `docs/hyperpowers`, deliberately keeping the approved spec as an uncommitted, git-ignored working file. Surprising for a document meant to be a durable design record; also means the spec would be lost on a clean checkout.

The brainstorming interview was long: 5 AskUserQuestion rounds (7 questions) plus two in-chat approval requests before the spec appeared; total ~12 minutes of wall clock for a brief described as small.
Multi-select tooling question required arrow-navigating past a hidden 'Type something' row to reach Submit; the Submit affordance is easy to miss in the list.

criteria.evidence: Session log jq over ce190780-...jsonl tool_use entries, first entry: "Skill|hyperpowers:brainstorming", preceding all Read/Write calls.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL; spec doc written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ before approval
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-logging-subsystem-design.md (not committed)." and later "Spec approved. The architectural path's terminal state is the planning skill". On disk: `wc -l docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-logging-subsystem-design.md` → 268 lines, beginning "# Logging Subsystem Design ... Status: approved design, not yet implemented".

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before I write the implementation plan." Prior to that, `find . -type f` in the workdir listed only index.html, README.md, package.json, app.js, src/index.js, src/utils.js — no new source files; log Write calls were only the spec, .gitignore, and codex-review scratch prompts.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Agent said "Both answers escalate the design" and "No code until the spec is approved", then created docs/hyperpowers/specs and committed the design to a file; no "this looks bounded" text appeared on screen.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe/spike plan appeared; the flow went interview → design options A/B/C → spec document → hyperpowers:writing-plans (log entry "Skill|hyperpowers:writing-plans").
